_comment: t/3646 — SSOT MIRROR of main's required status checks. This file is a DESCRIPTION, not
the source of truth. GitHub branch protection is AUTHORITATIVE:
gh api repos/AI-Rosetta-Stone/ai-triad-research/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks
Hand-editing this file changes NOTHING real — it only changes what workflow-lint enforces.
operations/devops/Test-RequiredContextsListDrift.ps1 validates this list against the live
API; that drift-guard MUST be green on main BEFORE the workflow-lint required-context rule
is promoted from warn-only to blocking (a lint enforcing a stale mirror is worse than none).
CodeQL (t/4567): the required context was 'CodeQL', posted by the GitHub CodeQL App as an
AGGREGATE status, not by a job in codeql.yml. That native alert-gating check never reports on
a merge-group ref (gh-readonly-queue/*), so the first real merge-queue batch stalled on it
indefinitely. Swapped to 'CodeQL Analysis' — the job-level check (codeql.yml's 'analyze' job),
which DOES fire reliably on merge_group — and alert-gating is restored at the RULESET level via
a 'code_scanning' rule (tool CodeQL, security_alerts_threshold high_or_higher), proven live-fire
on app-scratch (clean group merges; a group with a planted high-severity alert is refused at
enqueue, both for a pending and a failed analysis). No 'posts' marker now — R2/R5's job lookup
finds 'analyze' (posted name 'CodeQL Analysis') directly, same as any other job-level context.
'posts': 'app-aggregate' remains a valid marker for any FUTURE app-posted required context; it is
just not what CodeQL uses anymore. The R2/R5 job lookup is name-then-id (workflow-lint
_find_reporting_job, t/3691).
t/3804 PR-1: 'strict' is the SSOT's declared expectation for required_status_checks.strict —
Test-RequiredContextsListDrift.ps1 reads this field and compares it against the live API (already
present in the payload it queries; no endpoint change). Expected false: a stale-base PR must stay
mergeable without being forced to rebase against every main push (t/3686). strict:true here would
be a REGRESSION, not a hardening someone forgot to declare.
t/3804 PR-2: 'enforce_admins' is the SSOT's declared expectation for the PARENT /protection
endpoint's enforce_admins.enabled (NOT present in required_status_checks — a second gh api call
reads it; see Test-RequiredContextsListDrift.ps1). Expected true: per root AGENTS.md Pre-Self-Merge
Verification, this setting currently substitutes for two inert feedback rules (pre-self-merge-verify,
auto-merge-jointgv-guard; t/3695) by binding branch protection to admins too. enforce_admins:false
here would be a REGRESSION that silently re-opens both incident classes (t/3804).
t/4567 C2 (SO e/387#2, TL-accepted e/387#3): alert-gating now lives ONLY in the
'main-merge-queue' ruleset's own 'code_scanning' rule, not in classic protection — disabling
that ruleset silently drops alert-gating with classic protection looking unchanged (see the
Coupling warning in deploy/azure/runbooks/merge-queue-switch.md). merge_queue_ruleset below is
the declared expectation Test-RequiredContextsListDrift.ps1 checks against the live ruleset:
enforcement must be 'active' AND a matching code_scanning rule must be present.
